description: Eleanor's case with realistic friction: first supplier not taking Medicare patients, one out of stock, one no-answer-then-yes that later goes silent, PCP office loses the first request, patient misses the first update call. Unscripted suppliers never pick up.

supplier_screen.transcript:
Supplier: Lakeshore Home Medical, this is Dana.
Agent: Hi Dana, this is Mira, an automated care coordinator calling on behalf of a patient, Eleanor Martinez. She has Original Medicare Part B and needs a standard manual wheelchair, K0001. Are you taking new Medicare patients?
Supplier: We're enrolled with Medicare, yeah, but honestly we stopped taking new Medicare patients last month. Our billing person left and we're backed up. Maybe try us again in a couple of months.
Agent: Understood, thank you for your time.

Supplier: Lincoln Park DME, Marcus speaking.
Agent: Hi Marcus, this is Mira, an automated care coordinator calling for Eleanor Martinez. Original Medicare, no supplemental. She needs a standard manual wheelchair, K0001, delivered to 60614. Are you taking new Medicare patients and do you have one in stock?
Supplier: Yep, we take Medicare. 60614 is right down the street from us. We've got a few of the basic K0001 chairs on the floor.
Agent: Great. How soon could you deliver once you have the signed order?
Supplier: Two, three days tops. Send the order over and we'll get her on the schedule.
Agent: So I can tell her you'll take her on?
Supplier: Yeah, put us down.

Supplier: Halsted Home Health.
Agent: Hi, this is Mira, calling on behalf of a Medicare patient who needs a standard manual wheelchair, K0001, in 60614. Are you taking new Medicare patients?
Supplier: We are. The K0001s though, we're out. Manufacturer's got us on backorder, they're saying three weeks, could be longer. We could put her on the list.
Agent: Thanks, I'll note that.

Supplier: Prairie State Medical, this is Priya.
Agent: Hi Priya, this is Mira, an automated care coordinator for Eleanor Martinez, Original Medicare Part B. She needs a standard manual wheelchair, K0001, delivered to 60614. Are you taking new Medicare patients?
Supplier: We are. And we stock K0001, we've got plenty.
Agent: Do you deliver to 60614?
Supplier: We cover the whole north side, so yes. Usually about four days after we get a signed order and verify eligibility.
Agent: Can I confirm you'll take her case?
Supplier: Sure, happy to. Just get us the written order.

supplier_followup.transcript:
Supplier: Prairie State Medical, Priya.
Agent: Hi Priya, Mira again, following up on Eleanor Martinez's K0001 wheelchair.
Supplier: Oh yes, we got the order from Dr. Chen's office this morning. Eligibility checks out. She's on the truck for Tuesday, so about four days.
Agent: Perfect, thank you.

pcp_order_request.transcript:
Office: Sunrise Family Medicine, this is Maria.
Agent: Hi Maria, this is Mira, an automated care coordinator for Eleanor Martinez, date of birth on file. Dr. Chen saw her three days ago and noted a verbal order for a standard manual wheelchair. We need the written order so a Medicare supplier can deliver it.
Office: Let me look... okay, I see the note. I'll send it over to Dr. Chen's MA to prep the order. Usually takes a couple of days for her to sign.
Agent: Thank you. Who should I follow up with?
Office: Just ask for me, Maria.

pcp_order_nudge.transcript:
Office: Sunrise Family Medicine.
Agent: Hi, this is Mira following up on a written wheelchair order for Eleanor Martinez. I spoke with Maria a couple of days ago.
Office: Maria's out today. Let me check... I don't see any order request for her in the queue. Nothing came through to Dr. Chen. Are you sure it was sent?
Agent: It was requested by phone. Can I resend it?
Office: Fax it to 312-555-0199, attention Dr. Chen's MA, and we'll take care of it.

Office: Sunrise Family Medicine, Maria speaking.
Agent: Hi Maria, Mira again about Eleanor Martinez's wheelchair order.
Office: Yes, sorry about the mix-up. We got your fax. Dr. Chen signed it this morning and we faxed it to the supplier and back to you.
Agent: Thank you so much.

Office: Sunrise Family Medicine, Maria.
Agent: Hi Maria, it's Mira. We received Dr. Chen's order for Eleanor Martinez, but it's coded K0003, a lightweight wheelchair, and the NPI is missing. Medicare will deny it as written. She needs a standard manual wheelchair, K0001.
Office: Oh no, the MA must have picked the wrong template. Let me grab Dr. Chen... okay, she's corrected it to K0001, added her NPI and re-signed. I'm faxing it now.
Agent: Thank you, I'll watch for it.

patient_update.transcript:
Patient: Hello?
Agent: Hi Mrs. Martinez, this is Mira, the automated care coordinator working on your wheelchair. Your doctor's office is preparing the written order and we've found a supplier who can deliver.
Patient: Oh good. But am I going to get a bill for the whole chair? I really can't afford that.
Agent: Medicare Part B covers most of it. You'd typically owe about 20 percent.
Patient: Twenty percent of what though? Nobody told me a number. And will someone show me how to fold it?
Agent: I'll make sure someone follows up on both of those.

Patient: Hello?
Agent: Hi Mrs. Martinez, it's Mira. Your wheelchair is scheduled for delivery Tuesday from Prairie State Medical Supply. You'll owe about 20 percent of the Medicare-approved amount, and the supplier will bill you after delivery.
Patient: Tuesday, okay. Twenty percent, they'll send the bill. Got it, thank you dear.
